summary: Any position in an all-zero array can be changed to one and alter the maximum product, so a correct algorithm must inspect all n values in the worst case. The two-extreme DP matches that bound.

optimality.argument: For an all-zero array, the maximum subarray product is zero. If an algorithm leaves any position unread, changing only that value to one preserves the source constraints but changes the answer to one. Exact computation therefore requires Omega(n) inspections in the worst case. The current recurrence performs constant arithmetic and comparisons per value, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Changing any unseen zero to one changes the required result while every inspected value remains identical.
Each array value updates the ending maximum, ending minimum, and global best with constant work.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a negative sign change, a zero reset, and the noncontiguous-subsequence trap; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
